findings.claim: Securities fraud class action Patel v. Snowflake Inc. (No. 26-cv-01613, N.D. Cal.) filed on behalf of purchasers June 27 2023 - Feb 28 2024, alleging Snowflake and former top executives violated the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 by making false/misleading statements about tiered storage pricing and customer efficiency gains impacting consumption/revenue; triggered by the Feb 28 2024 withdrawal of the $10B 2029 product-revenue target and guidance cut to 22% YoY growth (stock fell 18.14%). Lead plaintiff deadline was April 27 2026.
findings.source: Kessler Topaz case page (ktmc.com/snow-snowflake-inc-class-action-lawsuit); Schall Law Firm notice via GlobeNewswire, 2026-04-20

findings.claim: Multidistrict litigation 'In Re: Snowflake, Inc. Data Security Breach Litigation' (MDL 3126, D. Mont.) consolidates federal cases over the April-June 2024 breach affecting Snowflake corporate customer accounts (AT&T, Advance Auto Parts, Cricket Wireless, Ticketmaster/Live Nation, Neiman Marcus, LendingTree's QuoteWizard), allegedly exposing personal data of 500M+ individuals. Parties agreed to material settlement terms Feb 1 2025 and filed a Notice of Settlement / Joint Motion to Stay All Deadlines Feb 3 2025; consolidated complaint filed on/about April 30 2025.
findings.source: D. Montana court case page (mtd.uscourts.gov/snowflake-data-security-breach-litigation); JPML transfer order; classaction.org settlement agreement filings

findings.claim: Snowflake reported Net Revenue Retention of 126% for Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended July 31, 2026), reported in the earnings release filed as an 8-K exhibit.

Q2 FY2027 total revenue $1,546.8M (+35% YoY), product revenue $1,491.9M (+37% YoY, accelerating for a third consecutive quarter); non-GAAP operating margin 15% (+400bps YoY); full-year FY2027 guidance raised to non-GAAP operating margin 14.5% (from 13.5%) and adjusted FCF margin reiterated at 23%. Rule-of-40 style sum (revenue growth + non-GAAP op margin, or + FCF margin) is well above 40 (35%+15%=50 or 35%+23%=58) on this quarter's disclosed metrics.
findings.source: SEC 8-K exhibit fy2027q2earnings.htm; Seeking Alpha 2026-09-02 ('Snowflake signals FY2027 product revenue of $6.07B with 14.5% non-GAAP operating margin guidance')

findings.claim: Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended July 31, 2026) total stock-based compensation expense was $456.4M, equal to 29.5% of total revenue ($456.4M / $1,546.8M), including ~$23.6M of employer payroll tax-related expense on employee stock transactions.
Weighted-average diluted shares outstanding: 377.9M in Q2 FY2027 (ended July 31, 2026) vs 372.4M in Q2 FY2026 (ended July 31, 2025) — YoY growth of ~1.5%.

Snowflake set a target (announced at its June Investor Day) for stock-based compensation to decline to about 27% of revenue in FY2027 (full-year target, vs the 29.5%-of-revenue print in the Q2 print above, indicating the full-year average is expected to trend down through the rest of FY2027).
findings.source: Aggregator summary citing Snowflake Investor Day commentary (surfaced via WebSearch; primary Investor Day deck not directly fetched)

findings.claim: Snowflake remains GAAP-operating-loss-making: Q2 FY2027 GAAP operating loss was ($263.0)M, driven substantially by stock-based compensation ($456.4M in the quarter, 29.5% of revenue). Full-year FY2027 guidance is framed only in non-GAAP terms (non-GAAP operating margin raised to 14.5% from 13.5%); no explicit GAAP net-income breakeven date or timeline was found in company guidance or the Q2 earnings call materials searched.

At its 2026 Investor Conference, CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy laid out a revenue roadmap (not a profitability roadmap) of $5B+ product revenue in FY2027, $7-8B by FY2029, and $10B by FY2030; this roadmap was framed around growth/AI-product mix rather than a specific GAAP profitability milestone.
findings.source: snowflake.help summary of Snowflake Investor Conference 2026 ('AI Growth Strategies & $10B Revenue Roadmap') — secondary aggregator, primary Investor Day transcript not directly fetched
